headline: Security and sandboxing for running untrusted code covers eleven tickets; six are backed by code we could read (process containment, resource caps, network blocking, certificate trust, the policy rule engine), while five could not be confirmed from the material reviewed.
what_is_there: The code shows working containment for risky commands — isolated Windows processes with CPU, memory and disk caps, network access blocked by default, and a configurable policy file that routes commands to different sandbox strengths by risk level. There is also a rules-driven security policy layer that feeds guardrail text into prompt, attachment and command checks, per-host certificate trust with a CA bundle override, and action logging of tool calls, permission decisions and sandbox attempts.
what_is_unclear: Five items could not be settled from the subset of code examined: the Hyper-V-based Windows Sandbox (configured as enabled, but no launching code was seen), prompt-injection detection and fencing, role-based permissions for workspaces and tasks, the retention/cleanup half of the audit log, and the ongoing rulebase review, which by its nature leaves no code trace. Two further notes: the ticket about file integrity verification is matched by code that does Windows privilege isolation rather than file checksums, and the URL-guard and macro-blocking parts of the network ticket were not seen.
suggested_action: Ask the team to confirm three things specifically: whether the Hyper-V sandbox actually launches, whether audit logs are ever pruned, and whether the file-integrity ticket was reworded to mean privilege isolation. Also confirm the certificate trust ticket can be closed, since the code looks finished while the tracker still shows it in progress.
